ai.en: The Saturday Farmers' Market in the redeveloped North Building of St. Lawrence Market, with seasonal produce, baked goods, meat, cheese and flowers.

events.description: Visit the Saturday Farmers' Market in the newly redeveloped St. Lawrence Market North building. Discover seasonal produce, baked goods, meats, cheeses, flowers and pantry staples from local vendors all under one roof.

title.en: Saturday Farmers' Market at Evergreen Brick Works

ai.en: The Saturday Farmers' Market at Evergreen Brick Works, one of Toronto's largest year-round markets, with Ontario produce and artisan goods.

events.description: Discover Toronto’s largest year-round farmers' market. Shop fresh, seasonal produce, artisanal goods and locally prepared foods from Ontario farmers and small businesses. Grab a coffee, wander through a vibrant market bursting with peak-season flavours and one-of-a-kind finds, and then enjoy a delicious brunch. Held in an open-air pavilion, the market runs rain or shine. Stick around to enjoy a free guided tour of the historic brick factory, take a stroll around the ponds and nearby nature trails or explore the Children's Garden. Getting there is easy with the free shuttle bus picking up next to Broadview Station or take the TTC's 28 bus from Davisville Station. The farmers' market is operated by Evergreen, a national non-profit transforming public spaces in our cities to build a healthier future for people and our planet.
events.address: 550 Bayview Ave, East York, ON, M4W 3X8

title.en: The Stop Farmers' Market @ Wychwood Barns Park

ai.en: The Stop Farmers' Market at Wychwood Barns Park, with more than 35 weekly vendors and a focus on healthy food access.

events.description: Featuring 35+ weekly vendors, the market brings together local farmers, food producers, and neighbours to increase access to healthy food in ways that build community. A program of The Stop Community Food Centre, the market supports both emerging and established small-scale producers while strengthening a resilient local food economy through responsibly grown and produced food. The market is committed to affordability, supporting racialized vendors, and creating welcoming, community-driven public spaces. Reflecting the diverse cultures of the neighbourhood and the broader GTA, the market celebrates the many food traditions that make Toronto vibrant. Come visit and support our year-round community market operating every Saturday in the Bathurst–St. Clair neighbourhood.

ai.en: Yesterday. Today. Forever., an outdoor walk through art installations across ten Mount Pleasant Cemetery sites and several funeral centres.

events.description: Walk through a series of artistic and interpretive installations across ten cemetery sites and several funeral centres. Across the participating sites, visitors will encounter a constellation of experiences, including interpretive panels, meditative spaces, soundscapes, experimental film, symbolic thresholds, and opportunities to leave a message of their own. Cemeteries bring generations into conversation. They hold names, trees, monuments, rituals, and traces of lives that still shape the world around us. The project invites visitors to reflect on how grief, memory, nature, design and community shape the places we inherit and the futures we share.

ai.en: The Junction Farmers' Market at Baird Park, with local, sustainably grown food and a supportive community.

events.description: Step into the lively Junction Farmers Market, where every visit is a celebration of fresh, local, and sustainably produced food! Join a vibrant community supporting passionate growers and producers while discovering delicious finds around every corner. Experience the joy of healthy, accessible food for everyone in and around the Junction—your next great food adventure starts here!
events.address: 275 Keele St, Toronto, ON M6P 2K5, Canada

ai.en: The Withrow Park Farmers' Market near Danforth Avenue in Greektown, running every season since 2006.

events.description: Just steps from Danforth Avenue in vibrant Greektown, Withrow Park Farmers’ Market bursts to life every season! Since 2006, it’s been the go-to destination for fresh food, lively music, local art, and a joyful sense of community—celebrating the best of Toronto while championing local farmers, producers, and artisans. From June to October, the park transforms into a buzzing hub of delicious discoveries and vibrant connection. We’re passionate about creating an inclusive, sustainable, and community-powered market where every visit is an adventure—and everyone’s welcome!

ai.en: Dancing Blossoms by Paula Hartmann at the Clark Centre for the Arts, a kinetic installation of paper mobiles that sway like spring trees.

events.description: Delight in Paula Hartmann's Dancing Blossoms, a kinetic installation composed of dozens of delicate paper mobiles suspended in air, evoking the quiet poetry of spring trees swaying in the wind. Crafted from featherlight paper and fine wire, each mobile captures a fleeting moment of bloom, movement, and renewal. About the Artist Paula Hartmann is a Canadian visual artist whose joyful, kinetic sculptures transform humble materials into poetic, suspended worlds. Based in Toronto and originally from Germany, she draws on cultural traditions, folk aesthetics, and contemporary design to create works that explore impermanence, transformation, and belonging. Often incorporating paper, wire, and natural elements, her mobiles and installations invite viewers into moments of play, presence, and quiet wonder. Her installations have been featured in major public art events, including Toronto’s Nuit Blanche, the Burlington Waterfront Sculpture Trail, and City of Craft Toronto.

ai.en: Turning in the Light at the Clark Centre for the Arts, Katharine Harvey's work on historic stone carvings rescued from demolished Toronto buildings, displayed at Guild Park.

events.description: Be inspired by Katharine Harvey's new body of work which explores the remarkable architectural fragments preserved at Guild Park. Historic stone carvings rescued from demolished Toronto buildings now coexist with forests, gardens and Lake Ontario. Through vibrant paintings, Harvey reveals layered stories that connect built heritatge, nature and memory, inviting viewers to see the park with fresh eyes. About the Artist Katharine Harvey is a Canadian conceptual painter and multi-media artist based in Toronto. Throughout her career, she has switched naturally between mediums, allowing her paintings to inform her public artwork and vice versa. This process inspired Katharine to create a body of work that includes multi-layered acrylic paintings, recycled plastic installations, monumental public art, kinetic sculptures and an illuminated drone show.

ai.en: Patterns That Aren't, an exhibition at Cedar Ridge Creative Centre by David Currie on how people seek out patterns to adapt to their surroundings.

events.description: Step into the intricate world of artist David Currie as he explores how humans are hard-wired to seek out patterns as a means of adapting to their environment, whether connecting imaginary lines to stars or writing algorithms that direct a robot’s movements. But once a pattern is understood, interest tends to fade. Here, Currie has developed a refreshingly new visual vocabulary, one built to engage rather than fade into the background in his series of large-scale, mixed media, papercut artworks that combine recent discoveries in mathematics with a lifetime of the artist’s skill, development and commitment.

ai.en: A free Boo Barn family afternoon at Riverdale Farm with a haunted house, games and face painting.

events.description: Enjoy a free family afternoon at Riverdale Farm dressed up for spooky season. Activities include a haunted house, children’s games, face painting and more. Meet at the Meeting House to experience the haunted house. Meet at the Francey Barn for pumpkin carving, apple cider, cookies and soda. Get active with line dancing from 1 to 3 p.m. at the Francey Barn Meet the Riverdale Farm farmer to learn about the farm animals: Goats at noon and sheep at 2 p.m.

ai.en: Cowboys and Wallflowers at Assembly Hall Gallery, collages that challenge gender roles and domestic expectations.

events.description: Immerse in collages that blend iconic imagery and wit to challenge gender norms and domestic expectations. Despite shifting gender dynamics, her work highlights ongoing struggles over household roles. Each piece is meticulously handmade from vintage materials dating 1800s–1970s by Danielle Colle. About the Artist Danielle Cole is a Toronto-based artist whose collages, composed of vintage graphics, examine domestic roles and consumerism. Her work has been exhibited internationally and featured in CBC Arts, Kolaj Magazine and Toronto Life.
events.address: 1 Colonel Samuel Smith Park Dr, Etobicoke, ON, M8V 4B6

ai.en: Ritual and Still Without Shelter, a dual exhibition at Ascent Gallery by James Rose and Emmanuel Udeh that examines how we see the human body and how physical change shapes perception.

events.description: Visual perceptions of the human gaze are analysed in this dual exhibit created by James Rose and Emmanuel Udeh. Rose depicts various forms of body modification to demonstrate how physical changes can have a sacred, transformative, spiritual effect that exceeds the body’s limitation. Udeh creates technically skilled, conceptually grounded drawings that balance realism with imagination; quiet yet powerful visual meditations explore what it means to watch and be watched. Reception: August 15, 2–4 p.m.
events.address: 399 The West Mall, Etobicoke, ON, M9C 2Y2

ai.en: The Allan Gardens Saturday Farmers' Market at the Children's Conservatory, with fresh produce and small-scale producers.

events.description: Celebrate local food, community, and sustainable agriculture. Discover fresh produce, artisanal products, and small-scale producers - all while connecting with the people who grow and create them.We invite you to come meet the vendors, discover new favourites, and taste the heart of your community! The Allan Gardens Farmers’ Market facilitates a direct exchange between local farmers, food producers, artisan makers, and consumers. Everything sold at the market (50%+1) must be grown, sourced, made, and/or prepared in Toronto and the surrounding area—ensuring that every purchase supports your neighbourhood economy. Join us year- round every Saturday from 10am-2pm, in the beautiful Allan Gardens Children’s Conservatory & Teaching Garden.

ai.en: The Sunday Variety Market at St. Lawrence Market's Big White Tent, now open every Saturday and Sunday as a weekend treasure hunt.

events.description: Get ready for the ultimate weekend treasure hunt! The Sunday Variety Market is now open every Saturday and Sunday, bringing the city’s biggest and most exciting market experience to life each week. Discover over 75 incredible vendors—dive into vintage fashion from every era, luxury finds, one-of-a-kind handmade goods, unique gifts, antiques, collectibles, sparkling jewelry, and local gems you won’t find anywhere else. Shop vintage like a true Toronto insider under the iconic big white tent and experience the city’s most vibrant small business community in the heart of downtown! If you’re looking for weekend plans in Toronto, don't miss this free event St. Lawrence Market - Toronto's most historic cultural destination.

title.en: Rebirth: The Quiet Becoming Installation at Fort York

ai.en: Rebirth: The Quiet Becoming, an outdoor installation at Fort York by Delali Cofie and Yuma Dean Hester, reimagining the site's layered history beside the Gardiner Expressway.

events.description: Experience a bold new outdoor installation on the Gardiner Expressway beside Fort York Visitor Centre. Created by artists Delali Cofie and Yuma Dean Hester, it reimagines the site’s layered histories through contemporary art. An accompanying exhibition inside the Visitor Centre deepens the experience, inviting visitors to encounter the Fort as a living cultural landscape shaped by reflection, dialogue and collaboration.
events.address: 250 Fort York Blvd, Toronto, ON, M5V 3K9

title.en: Trick or Trees Planting Event: Masseygrove Park

ai.en: A Trick or Trees planting day at Masseygrove Park, planting native trees and shrubs in costume.

events.description: Join us for a Halloween planting event at Masseygrove Park! Enhance our urban tree canopy by planting native trees and shrubs. Costumes are encouraged. Event site conditions vary. Contact us for more information including accessibility. If you would like to request accessibility support, contact us as soon as possible.

ai.en: Mini Mission: The Haunted Edition at Pocket Planet Canada, a Halloween game of 16 animated scenes inspired by iconic horror films and TV.

events.description: Something strange is lurking around this Halloween! Take on the mission and search for 16 all-new animated scenes inspired by iconic Halloween movie, TV and pop culture moments. Follow the visual clues and see how many you can find. Suitable for all ages. Miniature scenes are designed to be fun and playful rather than frightening. A few pop-up haunted house-style displays can be avoided. Parents and caregivers are encouraged to use their discretion based on their child’s comfort level with Halloween content. No actors or jump scares from actor interaction.

ai.en: The Good Mourning Festival at Evergreen Brick Works, a public festival that makes space for grief to be expressed and shared.

events.description: A public festival that brings grief and mourning out of the shadows and into the light. On the first day, we create a space where grief can be expressed, shared and understood through workshops, art installations, music, peer support and more. The second day of the festival is our Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) celebration. A Mexican and Latin American tradition, this day bring rituals, performances, crafts and food to commemorate loved ones who have died and embrace death as a universal part of life.
events.address: 550 Bayview Ave, East York, ON, M4W 3X8

title.en: 4th Annual United Way Haunted Garden Walk

ai.en: The 4th annual United Way Haunted Garden Walk at the Rosetta McClain Gardens, a self-guided Halloween trail for families.

events.description: It's spooky season at the Rosetta McClain Gardens. The gardens are transformed into a fun and spooky Halloween experience for families, children and community members to enjoy a self-guided tour. Entry is free but donations of any amount are accepted. All donations collected go directly to the United Way.
events.address: 5 Glen Everest Rd, Scarborough, ON, M1N 1J2

ai.en: BooFest at Cloverdale Mall, a Halloween event with a haunted house, carnival games and treats.

events.description: This Halloween extravaganza combines the enchanting allure of our spine-tingling haunted house, thrilling carnival games, delectable treats, and so much more! Whether you're donning your most mysterious mask, navigating our corn maze, trying your luck at our games, or savouring delectable culinary delights, we promise a spooktacular experience for all ages. Join us and become part of the fun!

ai.en: Portent by Tanya Marcuse at The Image Centre, a multichannel video of ominous natural scenes such as swaying trees and volcanic vapour.

events.description: Tanya Marcuse’s multichannel video Portent presents ominous scenes of the natural world: trees swaying in the wind, vapour rising from volcanic fumaroles, icy branches illuminated by flickering light, and other small disturbances that hint at forces beyond our understanding. The quiet is deliberate; the frame remains fixed while the environment shifts restlessly within it, evoking a tension between stillness and motion, beauty and unease, the known and unknown. Marcuse describes her work as an exploration of the kinship between disaster and the sublime, and of the ways the world around us is continually threatened, transformed, and made strange. Portent forms part of her expansive series Book of Miracles (2020-26), inspired by the Augsburger Wunderzeichenbuch, a 16th-century illuminated manuscript depicting natural disasters, supernatural phenomena, celestial spectacles and unexplained oddities.

title.en: Keeper’s Exhibit by Artist-in-Residence Kendra Yee

ai.en: Keeper's Exhibit by artist-in-residence Kendra Yee, a reimagined corner store that mixes personal stories with City of Toronto Archives research.

events.description: Experience a reimagined corner store that draws on artist Kendra Yee’s personal narratives alongside histories uncovered through research with the City of Toronto Archives. Together, these stories and materials honour Toronto’s history of Chinese-founded family businesses, represented as a series of new ceramic sculptures embedded with archival imagery that interpret objects commonly found in convenience stores. Rooted in Yee's exploration of her family's immigration to the Prairies during the era of the Chinese Head Tax and Chinese Exclusion Act, Keeper’s weaves household accounts with records of Toronto's Chinese community from the 1890s to the 1950s. The resulting installation is a journey of discovery, inviting visitors to consider the preservation of stories and the communities who shape them. Kendra Yee is the City of Toronto's Artist-in-Residence (2025 to 2026).

title.en: Sala-Manca Group: Like a Bird’s Nest

ai.en: Like a Bird's Nest, a retrospective of the Sala-Manca Group at PIX FILM Gallery, with installation, video and photography shown together for the first time.

events.description: Enjoy a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group. Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah, a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation. In their hands, the sukkah is interchangeably a ritual structure, an ethnographic object, a work of art, an ephemeral monument, a site of protest, and a performative arena. This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

events.description: A love letter to the classic crime thriller, Anthony Shaffer’s Sleuth is packed with razor-sharp dialogue and psychological games that will keep you guessing until the very end. When a celebrated mystery writer invites his wife’s lover to his secluded English country estate, what begins as a seemingly civilized encounter quickly spirals into a dangerous contest of wit and manipulation. But who is really in control, and who is playing whom? Directed by Peter Fernandes, this gripping production stars Patrick Galligan as Andrew Wyke and Sepehr Reybod as Milo Tindle, delivering a riveting battle of intellects in one of the most acclaimed suspense plays ever written. Whether you’re a lifelong fan of whodunits or discovering Sleuth for the first time, don’t miss this rare opportunity to experience a Shaw Festival production that honours the enduring legacy of classic suspense theatre. Part of the Shaw Festival at Harbourfront Centre.

events.description: Delve into stories of young people who were caught up in the violence of the Rebellion of 1837. Teenagers risked their lives on secret missions for their cause, volunteering on both sides of the rebellion. Some supported the revolutionaries while others defended the government of the day. Meet the young spies and secret agents, including the real life De Grassi kids and a mysterious rebel messenger who captured the attention of one of the world's most famous authors. title.en: Pressure: Growing Up After the Windrush - TIFF Cinematheque

ai.en: Pressure, a screening at TIFF Lightbox of Horace Ové's film about Afro-Caribbean life in Britain, marking 50 years since its festival premiere.

events.description: Coinciding with the 50th anniversary of the Festival of Festivals’ presentation of Horace Ové’s Pressure, this first Black British feature film celebrates the Afro-Caribbean diaspora’s rich contributions to British culture since their arrival on the HMT Empire Windrush. Curated by TIFF Cinematheque programmer Vicky Wong, this series explores the Windrush generation’s experience of systemic racism, intergenerational and cultural clash and its outsized influence on art, music and cinema that expanded British identity. In addition to Ové’s eponymous film, this series includes Lloyd Bradley’s Ten Bob in Winter (1963), Step Forward Youth (1977), Franco Rosso’s Babylon (TIFF ’81), Menelik Shabazz’s Burning an Illusion (1981), Maureen Blackwood and Isaac Julien’s The Passion of Remembrance (1986), Twilight City (TIFF ’89) from the Black Audio Film Collective and Steve McQueen’s Lovers Rock (2020). Pressure is presented in partnership with Windrush.

Follow the clues, solve the riddles, and help to decipher this most curious case. This 3-part event features: a talk by Ann McDougall, author of A Ghost In the Room; puzzle-solving and roleplaying while moving through different rooms of Spadina; Ghosts of My Friends, an early 20th century parlour game. This event is designed around a fictional scenario of real-life people. Topics include paranormal and death. The activities will involve some strong scents. The museum will be in low-light conditions and require guests to navigate through narrow pathways. For ages 13+.

events.description: Where Truth is Brought Into the Light, written by Danik McAfee. One Muskoka cottage. A yearly tradition of Friendsgiving and a whole lot left unsaid. Between the cocktails, questionable decisions, old flames, new lovers, and one increasingly chaotic evening, The Porch is a dark comedy mystery about chosen family and the ridiculous lengths we go to keep the peace. Set against a celebration built around gratitude, the play asks what happens when the stories holding us together begin to crack. Through an Indigenous lens, The Porch draws a parallel between the sanitized history of Thanksgiving and the histories we rewrite within our own families. Because eventually, the drinks run out, the party ends and everything buried finds its way into the light.

With fresh characters, familiar tales, and its twisted brand of terror, this site-specific theatrical experience brings literature’s most depraved characters to life and death. After a lady of the night is murdered, a mad doctor strikes a pact with the Devil to raise her from the dead. But all hell breaks loose when he comes face-to-face with her killer at a masquerade. Descend into madness with Victor Frankenstein, Henry Jekyll, and Dorian Gray to discover the results of playing God, and the monstrous repercussions when the Devil comes to collect. Celebrated American tenor Daniel McGrew is making his Canadian debut with Opera Atelier as Orpheus opposite French-Canadian soprano Mireille Asselin as Eurydice.

title.en: Richard Avedon: Immortal: Portraits of Aging

ai.en: Immortal: Portraits of Aging at The Image Centre, Richard Avedon's photographs of ageing across nearly fifty years.

events.description: For nearly half a century, celebrated American photographer Richard Avedon confronted one of portraiture’s enduring taboos: aging. From his earliest years at Harper’s Bazaar, Avedon broke with the conventions of idealized celebrity portraiture, revealing the marks of time on his subjects’ faces with unsparing clarity. Bringing together nearly 100 portraits made between the early 1950s and 2004, the exhibition features artists, writers, musicians and cultural icons including Toni Morrison, Gabriel García Márquez, Duke Ellington, Ronald Reagan, the Duke and Duchess of Windsor, Patti Smith, Truman Capote and the Dalai Lama. Immortal also includes a restaging of Avedon’s seminal 1974 Museum of Modern Art exhibition Jacob Israel Avedon, which chronicled his father’s final years in nine extraordinary portraits. Taken as a whole, the photographs reveal a lesser-known dimension of Avedon’s practice and offer an unprecedented exploration of aging through his distinctive vision.

Through research on Indigenous fashion history, cultural sustainability, and decolonial design practices, the exhibition highlights how contemporary Indigenous couturiers blend ancestral knowledge with cutting-edge innovation to redefine fashion on their own terms.

title.en: Retracing Tatreez: Palestinian Thobes through the Twentieth Century

ai.en: Retracing Tatreez at the Textile Museum of Canada, Palestinian thobes and embroidery from the 20th century, most shown for the first time.

events.description: Featuring several examples of Palestinian tatreez (embroidery) from the Textile Museum’s collection, most of which will be exhibited for the first time! Retracing Tatreez highlights what these belongings can tell us about the relationship between Palestinians and their homelands in the twentieth century and beyond. In this exhibition, curator Nina Rafique showcases these pieces with restored historical context and invites visitors to re-engage with their ways of storytelling. In doing so, Retracing Tatreez highlights what these embroideries can tell us about the unique regional connections between Palestinians and their homelands, as well as the journeys of these objects from the hands of their original creators to today.

ai.en: Planter by Deanna Armenti at High Park, a temporary eco-sculpture inspired by old-growth nurse logs, one of three across Toronto.

events.description: A temporary public art installation, Planter is an eco-sculpture inspired by the amorphous shapes of old growth forest nursery logs. Planter is one of three sculptures installed across Toronto for a project entitled Ecogenders. These three installations collaborate with their respective ecosystems to decay and regrow into the land. They are sites of transition and, in this way, outposts of possible gender expansive futures. The work is made of ethically sourced wood from urban trees around Toronto at the end of their life cycle. The sculpted form is achieved through a hybrid fabrication technique of digital machine milling and hand carving. Deanna Armenti (Fae/Faer, She/Her) is a Queer, Faegender interdisciplinary artist and researcher. She is a PhD candidate at Toronto Metropolitan University (TMU) in the Media and Design Innovation program. Deanna’s arts practice is a multimodal exploration of Transfuturist worldbuilding.

ai.en: Molly Steels: I Am/Was/Always at The Image Centre, photography on how images hold moments against death.

events.description: The philosopher Diana Prokofyeva considers a photograph to be a phenomenon that exists as a way to avoid death by copying a moment and suspending it within time - a way to be between two worlds:, the living and the dead. She suggests that a photograph gives confidence of existence, a way to state, “Here I am and was, and always shall have been.”. View this evolving series that looks to photography as a method of conceptualizing grief and mortality. Using family archives from the past century and conceptual imagery, I locate myself within a chain of human experience. I look to the women who came before me, observing the proof of their existence with reverence and the knowledge that I will one day add to this catalogue. Through this series I aim to overshadow existential fear with curiosity. Ephemeral aspects of nature are woven into this work as both an unrelenting force and a source of comfort.

events.description: An immersive exhibition that invites guests to step inside ancient Pompeii. Visitors can walk through a Pompeian house and city street, exploring spaces such as a bakery, a thermopolium (an ancient Roman commercial snack bar), a school, a tavern and baths. Guided by an original audio narrative, they can interact with everyday objects while discovering Roman water systems, medicine, food, fragrances and graffiti. Highlights include The Earth Remembers, a 200-square-metre immersive room tracing the city’s history and the eruption of Mount Vesuvius, and a Walking VR journey (only available for ages 7 and up) through the ancient city, including its shops, amphitheatre and coastline.

events.description: The Stephen Bulger Gallery is pleased to present there second solo exhibition of work by Geoffrey James, one of Canada’s pre-eminent photographers. James’s panoramic photographs explore the relationship between people and the landscapes they create, shape, and transform. He became known for using a panoramic camera to photograph gardens, parks, cities, mines, and other human-made environments. His photographs are carefully composed and largely devoid of people. His images of formal European gardens reveal the ways in which humans organize and control nature, while later photographs of places such as mines and borders explore the more destructive consequences of human intervention.

title.en: Turn of the Century: Elgar, Beach & Sibelius

ai.en: Turn of the Century at the George Weston Recital Hall, an afternoon of Elgar, Beach and Sibelius, three works from 1899.

events.description: An afternoon centered on three remarkable works composed in 1899, a pivotal year at the threshold of a new century. The program opens with Elgar’s Enigma Variations, a series of fourteen character sketches, each revealing a friend or colleague, tied together by a still-unsolved “hidden theme.” Anya Alexeyev then brings to life Amy Beach’s Piano Concerto, a work of lyricism and virtuosity that showcases the bold voice of one of America’s first internationally recognized female composers. The concert concludes with Sibelius’s Finlandia, a stirring tone poem whose melodies and dramatic climaxes evoke both the Finnish landscape and the fervor of a people yearning for freedom.

title.en: TIFA Presents East West Street: A Song of Good and Evil

ai.en: East West Street: A Song of Good and Evil at the Elgin and Winter Garden Theatres, a TIFA multimedia stage show based on Philippe Sands's book.

events.description: Based on Philippe Sands' award-winning book East West Street, this multimedia stage production has sold-out to audiences around the world. It blends the voice of Metropolitan Opera star Laurent Naouri and music by Bach, Rachmaninoff and Leonard Cohen with narration by Sands and French soprano Natalie Dessay. Reflecting on the theme of global justice, East West Street explores issues of morality, art, and humanity against the backdrop of three men whose lives intertwined during the Nuremberg trials. How do two people at the extremes of good and evil find solace in the same aria? Through the power of words and the beauty of music, East West Street delivers a provocative exploration of heartache and hope. This event is part of the 2026 edition of the Toronto International Festival of Authors. Find out more at festivalofauthors.ca.

ai.en: I'm Not a Comedian... I'm Lenny Bruce at the Leah Posluns Theatre, a play on the life of the comedian, which ran for 125 performances in Los Angeles.

events.description: A powerful theatrical performance detailing the life and struggles of legendary comedian Lenny Bruce. The production ran for 125 performances in Los Angeles and for nine months Off-Broadway, earning critical acclaim and rave reviews. Named an LA Times Critic’s Choice, the production explores the life and battles of one of the most groundbreaking and influential comedians of all time. Drawing from his many court battles in defense of free speech, the production also incorporates excerpts from his original comedic material and insights from his own writings. These elements are masterfully woven together by creator and star Ronnie Marmo and expertly directed by Tony Award-winning stage, film and television actor Joe Mantegna.

ai.en: Macbeth at Crow's Theatre, a solo performance of Shakespeare's tragedy about Macbeth's climb to power.

events.description: One prophecy. One performer. Total collapse. Shakespeare’s most haunting tragedy traces Macbeth’s ruthless climb to power in this solo performance, set against the cutthroat world of the modern tech industry. One prophecy sets the scene for Macbeth’s terrifying unraveling, where every thought, every fear, every choice pushes him beyond the point of no return. In this electrifying reimagining, the collision of unstoppable technology and human free will forces us to confront the fragility - and ferocity - of the human spirit. Discover what happens when the scale of a Shakespearean tragedy is transformed into a gripping ninety-minute performance. Evan Buliung, one of Canada's leading stage actors and veteran of twelve seasons at the Stratford Festival, returns to Crow's after his acclaimed performance as Pierre in Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812.

events.description: A book club party for readers who want conversation, connection, over a few cocktails. ​What happens when book lovers leave the group chat and meet in real life? A cozy-but-lively book club party designed for readers who want more than silent reading time. Expect playful games, short live readings, thoughtful conversation, special guest readers, book themed cocktail menu and a room full of people who love stories as much as you do. ​Bring a book you love, a passage you can’t stop thinking about or just your curiosity. Throughout the evening, we’ll mix and mingle over drinks, share favourite excerpts and explore the ideas, themes and moments that stay with us long after the last page. ​Whether you’re a casual reader, a deep-dive annotator or someone looking to meet thoughtful, creative people in the city — this night is for you.

ai.en: An opera gala recital by Ricardo Marinello at the George Weston Recital Hall.

events.description: Join us for an unforgettable evening of world-class music in Toronto at the Opera Gala Recital by Ricardo Marinello. This exceptional concert will feature a selection of the most beautiful and beloved opera arias, along with other outstanding classical pieces, performed live in an elegant and atmospheric setting. The program promises a rich journey through the masterpieces of opera, filled with emotion, drama, and virtuoso vocals. Ricardo Marinello is a renowned Italian tenor, internationally recognized for his powerful voice, lyrical expression, and captivating stage presence. He gained widespread fame after winning the popular German TV show "Das Supertalent", becoming one of the most celebrated classical crossover artists of his generation. Since then, he has performed on prestigious stages across Europe and beyond, enchanting audiences with his unique combination of operatic tradition and modern sensibility.

events.description: The celebrated French-Canadian cellist and French pianist reunite for an afternoon of refined artistry, performing works by Brahms, Debussy, Schubert, and others. Jean-Guihen Queyras learnt his interpretative approach from none other than Pierre Boulez, with whom his artistic partnership spanned many years. A flawless technique and a clear, decisive sound shapes his approach to every performance and his absolute commitment to the music itself. In a career spanning 25 years, Alexandre Tharaud has become a unique figure in the classical music world and a key exponent of French pianism. His extraordinary repertoire ranges from Couperin, Bach, and Scarlatti, through Mozart, Beethoven, Schubert, Chopin, Brahms, and Rachmaninov, to the major 20th century French composers.

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part romcom, part goofy If-This-Then-What story, and part dystopian exploration of class, gender, language, and communication in relationships. The show is Directed by Bonnie Duff and Produced by Bonnie Duff and Miranda Wiseman. Featuring Lara Lucia as Bernadette and Jack Copland as Oliver. Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie, Sound Design by Jake Schindler and Lighting Design by Jay Hines. Production Managed by Jeremy Hutton

events.description: DIYAR Shahram Nazeri | Kaykhosro Pournazeri | Tahmoures Pournazeri DIYAR is a landmark musical event bringing together three extraordinary figures of Iranian music: the legendary voice of Shahram Nazeri; Kaykhosro Pournazeri, Grand Master of the Tanbur and a pioneering figure in its revival; and acclaimed composer Tahmoures Pournazeri, whose contemporary compositions and innovative arrangements have connected Iran's rich musical heritage with a new generation of listeners. For the first time, Shahram Nazeri performs a new body of work composed by Tahmoures Pournazeri, following the remarkable reception of their collaboration, "Amoo Nowruz." Joined by internationally recognized musicians and vocalists, DIYAR brings together contemporary Iranian music, the mystical tradition of the tanbur, and the vibrant rhythmic energy of Kurdish music in a powerful live experience performed in Persian and Kurdish. Presented by TAR Production

events.description: Before the internet there was paper. Vintage paper in the form of rare and unusual books, handwritten letters, vintage postcards, maps, posters, photography, manuscripts and much more. So much paper has been lost over time, burned, trashed, rotted and disintegrated. But some of the best paper has survived and is treasured by people who find joy in collecting vintage paper in all its forms. A unique event showcasing ancient paper, eighty tables plied high, where a visitor can spend a leisurely hour or half day browsing through paper relics from another time. Categories include pulp fiction, old advertising, concert, travel, movie posters, rare books, first editions, maps, prints and genuine curiosities. title.en: ROM Speaks Kristallnacht "The Night of Broken Glass"

ai.en: ROM Speaks: Kristallnacht, The Night of Broken Glass, a one-night performance at the Royal Ontario Museum by Saul Rubinek and Seana McKenna.

events.description: Iconic Canadian Artists Saul Rubinek and Seana McKenna Perform for one night only. A must-attend night with Saul Rubinek and Seana McKenna, who will perform a dramatic reading from an original theatrical work to commemorate Kristallnacht. Referred to as "The Night of Broken Glass", Kristallnacht occurred on November 9 and 10, 1938 across Germany, Austria, and elsewhere in Europe when Nazis led gangs in the torching, vandalising, and ransacking of Jewish shops, businesses, and synagogues. This event is seen as the beginning of the Nazis' systematic attempt to annihilate Europe's Jewish population. Through vivid storytelling, each performer weaves their magic with the audience, inviting a compelling examination of the choices ordinary people make in extraordinary times. This exciting performance by Rubinek and McKenna, will be followed by a reception with the artists, and access to the Dr. Fred Weinberg and Joy Cherry Weinberg Judaica Gallery at ROM.

title.en: Hannaford Street Silver Band presents Requiem

ai.en: Requiem by the Hannaford Street Silver Band with the Amadeus Choir at Metropolitan United Church, a concert of contemporary music on remembrance and grief.

events.description: The Hannaford Street Silver Band joins with Amadeus Choir for a deeply moving evening of contemporary music exploring remembrance, identity, grief, and hope. At the heart of the program is Requiem for a Charred Skull, the extraordinary large-scale work by celebrated Canadian composer and conductor Bramwell Tovey. Written in response to the tragic loss of cultural heritage during the Bosnian War, the work combines immense emotional power with moments of profound tenderness, creating a gripping musical meditation on humanity's capacity for both destruction and resilience. The program also features Gi-Giwe Na? (Are you going home?) by Barbara Assiginaak, a poignant and evocative work that contemplates belonging, memory, and connection to home from an Indigenous perspective. Additional works include Exultations by acclaimed composer Reena Esmail, whose music bridges Western and Indian classical traditions with luminous colour and rhythmic vitality.

ai.en: A Christmas Carol at the Fleck at Harbourfront Centre Theatre, a fresh adaptation of Dickens's story by Tim Carroll.

events.description: Dickens’s timeless holiday story of transformation, kindness and human connection. This fresh adaptation by Tim Carroll brings Charles Dickens’s world to life through inventive puppetry, towering ghosts that fill the stage, traditional carols and audience participation with spirited sing-alongs. Interactive performers mingle throughout the theatre, while beautifully detailed period costumes and sets create an atmospheric Victorian Christmas. More than 175 years after Dickens first published A Christmas Carol, audiences still recognize themselves in Ebenezer Scrooge: someone who discovers that it’s never too late in life to choose kindness and human connection. For centuries, this iconic story has endured because its themes are still relevant today: What really matters to us? And can people truly change?

title.en: Rebellion Talks: Booze, Taverns & Rowdy Rebels - SOLD OUT

ai.en: Rebellion Talks: Booze, Taverns and Rowdy Rebels at Montgomery's Inn, on the taverns and politics before the Rebellion of 1837. Sold out.

events.description: Learn the role Toronto's raucous taverns played in the political tensions leading up to the Rebellion of 1837. In the middle of the 1800s, taverns played a central role in political life. Montgomery’s Inn served as a watering hole during those tense years, making it the perfect place to discuss Toronto’s tavern history and how these places helped set the stage for Mackenzie’s attempted revolution. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

ai.en: The Joint Tour by Hamilton Leithauser and Rostam at The Concert Hall, playing the album I Had a Dream That You Were Mine.

events.description: At the time I Had a Dream That You Were Mine was first released, the Hamilton Leithauser and Rostam were best known for their work in two of the most influential rock bands of the era: Hamilton as lead singer in The Walkmen and Rostam as the co-songwriter and producer behind Vampire Weekend. The inspired collaboration was born of friendship, and mutual admiration,but grew into a synergistic creative partnership that birthed a timeless album of beautifullyevocative songs. I Had a Dream That You Were Mineis a delightfully immersive album, built around Rostam's meticulous, expansive production and Hamilton's distinctive, wild vocal range. Unlike anything either artist had done before, the album's stylistic flourishes include doo-wop, country-rock, baroque pop, folk, and spellbinding torch songs. Together, the lauded musicians found a unique flair for the dramatic which made their handful of live performances a thrilling experience; ten years on, these rare live shows are not to be missed!

ai.en: A food walk through Scarborough's Agincourt area, known as Asiancourt, and its East Asian restaurants at Lang Chai Authentic Vietnamese Cuisine.

events.description: Agincourt, also lovingly known as ‘Asiancourt’, is the beating heart of East Asian dining in Toronto, where unassuming strip plazas hide some of the most dynamic regional cooking in North America. On this tour, we will follow the flavours and stories that have shaped Agincourt across generations: from the fragrant lemongrass and herb-infused noodle broths of Vietnam, to deeply comforting, slow-simmered Korean pork-bone stews. We'll explore how northern Chinese charcoal-grilling traditions took hold alongside Cantonese staples as we sample cumin-dusted skewers and smoky street-style barbecue, before ending on a sweet note with a rich, multi-textured matcha parfait!

CALIGARI is a 1920 German silent horror film, directed by Robert Wiene and written by Hans Janowitz and Carl Mayer. Considered the quintessential work of German Expressionist cinema, it tells the story of an insane hypnotist (Werner Krauss) who uses a somnambulist (Conrad Veidt) to commit murders. The film features a dark and twisted visual style, with sharp-pointed forms, oblique and curving lines, structures and landscapes that lean and twist in unusual angles, and shadows and streaks of light painted directly onto the sets. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IAtpxqajFak NASH THE SLASH composed the musical scores for these and several other classic silent films and would perform them live at each screening. title.en: Benedict Sheehan’s ‘Ukrainian War Requiem’: The National Tour

ai.en: Benedict Sheehan's Ukrainian War Requiem, a national tour at St. Paul's Basilica by the Axios Men's Ensemble, a Juno-winning group.

events.description: The Axios Men’s Ensemble, in celebration of their historic Juno award, for Classical Album of the Year (Large Ensemble) for the recording of Benedict Sheehan’s Ukrainian War Requiem, have announced a national tour this November. Composed by two-time Grammy-Nominated Benedict Sheehan, this monumental choral work spans 12 impactful movements that seamlessly blend modern musical styles with ancient chants and traditional Ukrainian motifs. The choral tribute serves as a powerful musical reverence for those affected by the war, offering solace and strength to the living and the grieving, and ultimately providing a solemn space for remembrance and prayer through a skillful and heartfelt tribute to Ukraine and her people. Conducted by Maestro Michael Zaugg, the choir features over 50 performers from Axios Men’s Ensemble, Pro Coro Canada and international soloists. More than music, Ukrainian War Requiem is a journey through grief that reminds us of the enduring grace of the human spirit.

events.description: Discover a lesser-known chapter of Canadian history celebrating democracy and solidarity at a special documentary screening. In 1991, approximately 80 young Canadians and Americans of Ukrainian descent, including many participants from Toronto, travelled to Ukraine to support its independence movement ahead of the December 1 referendum. Through rare archival footage and firsthand accounts, the documentary explores Canadian civic engagement, international solidarity and the power of individuals to advance democracy. On December 2, 1991, Canada became the first Western country to recognize Ukraine's independence. Thirty-five years later, the film highlights Toronto's connections to global history as Ukraine continues to defend its sovereignty. Join us on November 18 for a story of courage and civic responsibility, followed by a discussion and Q&A with the filmmakers.

The Naghash Ensemble combines the earthy spirituality of Armenian folk songs, new classical music, and contemporary post-minimalism with the energy of rock and jazz. Three brilliant female vocalists and some of Armenia’s finest instrumentalists on duduk, oud, dhol, and piano play captivating new music based on sacred texts by the medieval Armenian mystic poet and priest Mkrtich Naghash.

events.description: The Toronto Artists Symphony Orchestra presents an extraordinary evening of orchestral and piano masterpieces featuring internationally acclaimed pianist Sofia Gulyak, one of the most distinguished pianists of her generation and winner of numerous international awards. This captivating program brings together some of the most beloved works from the classical repertoire, highlighting the music of Tchaikovsky and Rachmaninoff. The evening also features the Suite from The Red Detachment of Women, one of the most celebrated and recognizable works in Chinese musical culture. title.en: Rebellion Talks: The Strange & Tragic Tale of Robert Baldwin

ai.en: A Rebellion Talks session at Spadina Museum on Robert Baldwin, a pivotal and unusual figure in Canadian political history.

events.description: Listen to the story of Robert Baldwin, one of the strangest and most pivotal figures in Canadian history. Not everyone who demanded change believed in violence. One of the leading champions of Canadian democracy refused to take up arms and join the rebels. Baldwin's summer home was located where the museum is today. Investigate the role Baldwin played in trying to find a peaceful solution to the rebellion crisis, how he eventually accomplished what Mackenzie never did, and the bizarre twist to his tragic love story. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

ai.en: Song for a Winter's Day at the Jane Mallett Theatre, a midwinter concert based on Susan Cooper's The Shortest Day.

events.description: Susan Cooper's The Shortest Day looks across centuries of midwinter tradition: fires burning through the night, homes hung with evergreen, and people singing and dancing against the dark. At the heart of CCOC's Winter Concert is a staged telling of Cooper's poem, woven throughout the performance. Choral music brings its imagery to life: from snowfall and candlelight to celebration and the promise of returning light. CCOC's young artists perform works by Marie-Claire Saindon, Katerina Gimon, Benjamin Britten, Amy Beach, John Beckwith and more, accompanied by live musicians. The concert also features the world premiere of Soir d'hiver by CCOC pianist Stéphane Mayer. Both performances conclude with a cherished company tradition: Gordon Lightfoot's Song for a Winter's Night, arranged by Chris and Charissa Bagan. Join us for a winter gathering alive with story, song and the joyful sound of young voices.

title.en: Curator’s Talk: Time, Labour and the Value of Beads

ai.en: A curator's talk at the Bata Shoe Museum on the history and value of beads, in connection with the Brilliant exhibition.

events.description: Beads may be small and intricate, but their histories reveal powerful stories of identity, value, and status. In celebration of Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear Around the World, join Director and Senior Curator Elizabeth Semmelhack for an informative and illuminating exploration of beadwork traditions from around the world and their role as markers of wealth, prestige, and cultural meaning. From royal adornment and ceremonial regalia to trade and personal expression, this lecture traces how beads have signaled belonging across time and place. At its core is the labour behind the work: the skilled craftsmanship, generational knowledge, and cultural practices embedded in every stitch. By centering time and labour, the talk challenges conventional ideas of value and asks what makes something “luxurious,” and who defines luxury.
events.address: 327 Bloor St W, Toronto, ON, M5S 1W7

events.description: Orison (prayer) is a musical collaboration from musician Daniel Áñez and composer James O’Callaghan, connecting science fiction imagery with spirituality and the idea of ‘alien-ness’ in all of its senses: social, cultural, psychological, extra-terrestrial. The work centres the unique early electronic instrument, the ondes Martenot, as a jumping-off point to interact with synthesized soundscapes, field recordings, techno, poetic text, and documentary-like spoken confessionals. Featuring Ánez on the incredibly evocative ondes Martenot, with O’Callaghan on electronics, this Encounters event presents the current musical stage in the development of a new music theatre work. Audiences will experience fragments, improvisatory excerpts, and other material from this long-term work in progress, offering a rare opportunity to engage with the creative process as the piece continues to evolve. Please join us for this unique musical experience.

events.description: NOVA: After The Music is a powerful new dance production inspired by the story of a survivor of the Nova Music Festival massacre on October 7, 2023. Through contemporary dance, music, and immersive theatrical storytelling, the production traces a journey from the freedom and joy of the festival through terror, survival, grief, and ultimately resilience. Grounded in a real survivor's experience, NOVA: After The Music is both a deeply personal story and a collective act of remembrance. The production honours the lives that were lost, gives space to the stories of those who survived, and explores what it means to carry memory forward after unimaginable loss. It is a moving tribute to life, humanity, and the enduring strength to keep dancing after the music stops.

events.description: Constantinople: Oum Kalthoum & the Quatrains of Khayyam The timeless poetry of Omar Khayyam meets the unforgettable musical world of Oum Kalthoum in this extraordinary performance by Constantinople with Ghalia Benali. Reimagined through Persian and Arabic musical traditions, early music, contemporary composition, and live improvisation, the performance brings poetry, voice, and music into conversation across centuries. Songs inspired by Khayyam's quatrains, composed by Riad El Sonbati and made famous through Oum Kalthoum's interpretations, become the starting point for a new artistic journey. Led by Iranian-Canadian composer and setar virtuoso Kiya Tabassian, Constantinople is joined by Tunisian-Belgian vocalist Ghalia Benali, whose deep connection to Oum Kalthoum's repertoire brings insight, presence, and a distinctive contemporary voice. This concert is part of Ishq Festival 2026, produced by Small World Music.

title.en: Hannaford Street Silver Band presents A Celtic Holiday

ai.en: A Celtic Holiday by the Hannaford Street Silver Band at Ada Slaight Hall, blending Irish and Scottish music with brass.

events.description: A Celtic Holiday blends the rich musical traditions of Ireland and Scotland with the brilliance of brass band sound for a festive concert unlike any other. Featuring acclaimed fiddler Dan MacDonald and beloved Irish vocalist Michael Darcy, the evening will transport audiences from cozy winter hearths to lively Celtic kitchens and dance halls. Traditional carols, soaring ballads, joyful jigs, and foot-stomping reels come together in a celebration of music, storytelling, and community. Adding to the excitement will be performances by Irish dancers whose dazzling footwork and infectious energy bring the music vividly to life. Audience participation will also be part of the fun, inviting concertgoers to sing along and join in the holiday spirit. Whether it's the nostalgic beauty of a traditional Irish melody, the exhilaration of a fast-paced fiddle tune, or the warmth of familiar seasonal favourites, A Celtic Holiday offers something for everyone to celebrate the holiday.

events.description: Held, by 2024 Scotiabank Giller Prize winner Anne Michaels, is a luminous, fragmented novel about love, memory, and the reverberations of war across generations. Beginning on a First World War battlefield, the narrative moves through time and place to explore how desire and grief endure beyond a single lifetime. Michaels – renowned poet and author of Fugitive Pieces—weaves history and intimacy into a work of haunting beauty. By the Lake Book Club hosts six Tuesday-night events from February to December with top Canadian authors and Humber Polytechnics alumni. Each in-person event features readings, discussions, Q&A, book signings and ASL interpretation, while virtual sessions include live subtitles and audio access.

title.en: Music Toronto - Gryphon Trio with James Campbell

ai.en: Music Toronto presents the Gryphon Trio with James Campbell at the Jane Mallett Theatre, playing Messiaen's Quartet for the End of Time.

events.description: In its early years as a Music Toronto ensemble-in-residence, the Gryphon Trio first performed Olivier Messiaen’s visionary "Quartet for the End of Time" with revered Canadian clarinetist James Campbell. Composed in a prisoner-of-war camp during the Second World War, the work stands as one of the 20th century’s most profound musical testaments of faith, transcendence and human resilience. Twenty-five years and countless performances later, the Gryphon Trio and Campbell return to this monumental masterpiece that has become a defining thread in their artistic story. The program opens with the stormy passion of Johannes Brahms’ dramatic Piano Trio in C minor and also features the world premiere of a new work for piano trio by Graham Campbell.

events.description: A journey into the realm of memory. Lepage plunges into the depths of memory and questions the relevance of certain recollections. Why do we remember the phone number from our youth, yet forget our current one? How does a childhood song withstand the test of time, while the name of a loved one escapes us? Why does meaningless information stay with us, while other, more useful information falls away? The show considers various commemorative markers and the historical heritage around us that we no longer notice. The play also focuses on oblivion, the unconscious and memory that fades over time, whose limits are now compensated for by digital storage, mountains of data and virtual memory. Somewhere between theatre performance and conference, Lepage reveals the suffering of an actor who must remember not only his text, but also his past, as well as the historical and social realities that have shaped his identity.

Join us for a single feature workshop or book both days to fully immerse yourself in handmade holiday creativity. Day 1: Contemporary Paper Quilling with Yuyo Paper Arts Experience the art of transforming paper with contemporary artist Oriana Castillo. title.en: Rebellion Talks: The Rebels' Island Stronghold

ai.en: A Rebellion Talks session at Todmorden Mills on the Rebels' island stronghold and the aftermath of the Rebellion of 1837.

events.description: Learn about the violent aftermath of the Rebellion of 1837. The revolutionaries didn't give up easily. Even after Mackenzie's army was crushed at the Battle of Montgomery's Tavern, the rebels kept fighting. They rallied new supporters as they seized control of an island in the Niagara River, declared it to be the independent Republic of Canada, and launched what became known as the Patriot War. It's a story of bloody battles, revolutionary spies, pirate admirals, and two competing visions for the future of the continent. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

ai.en: Sex in the '80s at the Berkeley Street Theatre, a play about two architects reunited after the 1980s.

events.description: Old history. New rules. They haven’t seen each other since the 1980s. Now two accomplished architects are reunited in a glass-walled Toronto office tower on the eve of a high-stakes competition. Both intend to keep things strictly professional. That proves harder than expected. As a long-buried chapter of their shared history resurfaces, a polite reunion turns into a pointed, funny sparring match about memory, ambition, and how much the rules have changed. Meanwhile, their twentysomething colleagues look on and aren’t shy about weighing in. Smart, topical, and wickedly witty, this is a workplace comedy about generational change and the risky business of revisiting the past.

title.en: License to Thrill: Music of James Bond

ai.en: License to Thrill: Music of James Bond, an afternoon concert by Orchestra Toronto at Meridian Arts Centre, with vocalists Heather Bambrick, Suzie McNeil and Gavin Hope performing Bond themes.

events.description: Orchestra Toronto invites you to an afternoon of cinematic excitement with the music of James Bond, featuring vocal performances by Heather Bambrick, Suzie McNeil, and Gavin Hope. From instantly recognizable themes that have defined the Bond legacy to reimagined orchestral interpretations of lesser-known gems, this program blends sophistication, swing, and cinematic drama. The singers bring each iconic melody to life, capturing the tension, glamour, and intrigue that make Bond?s music a classic. Join us for an experience where orchestral precision meets the thrill of the silver screen, celebrating some of the most memorable music in modern popular culture.

title.en: Bouchara: The Light of Other Worlds

ai.en: Bouchara: The Light of Other Worlds at the Temerty Theatre, Brian Current leads Glenn Gould School students in contemporary music, including Claude Vivier.

events.description: Brian Current leads Glenn Gould School students in bold contemporary music that opens imagined worlds. Enjoy pieces from Claude Vivier’s Bouchara to works by Hannah Kendall and Francis Battah. Bouchara, Vivier’s luminous work for soprano and ensemble, is widely recognized as one of his most beautiful and singular creations. Sung in an invented, intimate language, it opens a sound world that feels both ancient and deeply personal. Alongside it, shouting forever into the receiver by Hannah Kendall, one of today’s most compelling international voices, and Francis Battah’s Musique d’un monde sans carte, extend this sense of hidden worlds: places we cannot quite name, where sound becomes a space of memory, imagination and discovery.

Named by The Economist as one of Twenty Living Polymaths, Hough was the first classical performer to be awarded a MacArthur Fellowship (2001). He was awarded Northwestern University’s 2008 Jean Gimbel Lane Prize in Piano, won the Royal Philharmonic Society Instrumentalist Award in 2010. In 2014 he was made a Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) and was knighted in the Queen’s Birthday Honours in 2022.

events.description: The Bang on a Can All-Stars have collaborated and toured with fellow New Yorkers Philip Glass and Steve Reich for more than 30 years. This concert features Glassworks, exclusively arranged by Michael Riesman alongside Reich’s acclaimed rock-infused Electric Counterpoint for electric guitar, in honor of these two outstanding composers during their milestone 90th birthday year. In 1982 Philip Glass became the first composer since Aaron Copland to join the CBS Masterworks label. His first album for Masterworks, Glassworks, tripled all sales projections, and was lauded by audiences and critics alike. Celebrating the legendary composer’s 90th Birthday year as Bang on a Can All-Stars perform a brand-new arrangement of the iconic Philip Glass album in its entirety for the very first time.

title.en: Rebellion Talks: Riots & the Rebel Mayor

ai.en: A Rebellion Talks session at Mackenzie House on the riots that shook Toronto before and after the Rebellion of 1837.

events.description: Learn about the riots that shook Toronto to its core in the years before and after the Rebellion of 1837 in the rebel mayor’s former home, which is now Mackenzie House Museum. Political violence was a common occurrence in Toronto; rival factions battled in our streets. Hear the history behind the riots that helped convince Mackenzie that an armed revolution was his only option and explore the riots that continued to rage long after his rebellion was over. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

events.description: Marian Hill is an American electronic pop duo made up of vocalist Samantha Gongol and producer Jeremy Lloyd. Their sound blends moody electronics, jazz-influenced saxophone, and Gongol's distinctive vocals into a style that's sleek, intimate, and hard to categorize --- somewhere between R&B, pop, and avant-garde electronic music. They arrived on the scene in 2013 when their single , "rdquo" -> One Time" went viral on Vine. Before long, their song Got It was in one of the first Today's Top Hits playlists as well as a Taco Bell commercial, leading them to sign with Republic Records. They embarked on their first national tour and a radio campaign followed, peaking with One Time at #38 on US Alt Radio. Their big breakthrough came a few years later when their single "Down" was featured in Apple's AirPods ad, pairing Gongol's smoky vocals and a sparse piano line with a stuttering electronic beat --- making it one of the most Shazamed songs in the country. The track reached No. 21 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was recently certified double platinum. Their music has been in major commercials for All State, Calvin Klein, Hyundai and Fox Sports and seen on TV in HBO's Industry, Lucifer, Santa Clarita Diet, So You Think You Can Dance and Dancing with the Stars. They've performed at Coachella, Lollapalooza, Bonaroo, Electric Forest, Firefly, Governor's Ball, and more and played to sold out crowds abroad in China, Korea, Japan and all over Europe. title.en: Rebellion Talks: Mackenzie's Unlikely Montreal Allies

ai.en: A Rebellion Talks session at Colborne Lodge on the Lower Canadian rebellion and its links to the Rebellion of 1837 in Toronto.

events.description: Learn about the rebellion in Lower Canada (Québec) and its connection to the Rebellion of 1837 in Toronto. The rebellion in Toronto wasn't the only one. At the same time revolutionaries were taking up arms here, an even bigger rebellion was breaking out in Lower Canada. Meet the Lower Canadian rebels and learn about Mackenzie's relationship with them. Join the conversation at Colborne Lodge, the historic home in High Park named in honour of the governor those rebels in Québec were trying to overthrow. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

title.en: East Meets West: Harmony Across Cultures

ai.en: East Meets West: Harmony Across Cultures, an Orchestra Toronto concert at Meridian Arts Centre's George Weston Hall, with erhu player Amely Zhou and tabla player Razak Pirani.

events.description: Orchestra Toronto explores the meeting of tradition and innovation, featuring Amely Zhou on erhu and Razak Pirani on tabla. The concert opens with Reena Esmail?s Testament (from Vishwas), a work that blends Indian classical sensibilities with Western orchestral textures, exploring themes of memory, identity, and faith. Canadian composer Kevin Lau?s Between the Earth and Forever follows, a reflective and expansive piece that draws listeners into its meditative landscapes and delicate harmonies. The program concludes with Shostakovich?s Symphony No. 5 in D Minor, a masterwork of tension and resilience, whose dramatic contrasts and haunting motifs reflect the composer?s struggles under Soviet censorship while remaining a testament to human endurance and expressive power.

title.en: Rebellion Talks: Rebel Blacksmiths & Radical Farmers

ai.en: A Rebellion Talks session at the Scarborough Museum on rebel blacksmiths and radical farmers in 1837.

events.description: Consider the role of rebel blacksmiths and radical farmers in the Rebellion of 1837. As the rebellion approached, the countryside around Toronto was alive with farmers running military drills and blacksmiths forging weapons. Mackenzie's rebel army would include many ordinary people from the surrounding area who found themselves swept up in the cause. Head to Scarborough Museum to learn about the role civilians played in the uprising—and how two of them found themselves at the end of a hangman's noose. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

events.description: Every desire has a cost. At a secluded seaside hotel, a young artist and his magnetic wife find their marriage unsettled by the arrival of a charismatic stranger. events.description: Legal Age 19+ (Valid Photo I.D Required)For Love of Grace s tightest album to date, even glossy at times, but not tight enough to dull its pulse. With wordless howls, nastily detuned riffs that bend into harmony, breakdowns, handclaps, and a chaotic choral break seemingly played on pennywhistles, For Love of Grace s fundamental curiosity and trust in their instincts. Produced and mixed by the band (Rnnenfelt, Dan Kjr Nielsen, Jakob Tvilling Pless, Johan S. Weith, and Casper Morilla Fernandez) and Nis Bysted, For Love of Grace s Plowing Into the Field of Love at the same studio; its no coincidence its the only time they have returned to a studio to cut a record. The band wanted to capture the same intense energy. The band leaned on their experiences and the thousands of hours on stages theyve shared since they were teenagers. The setup was as minimal as possible: making decisions live and not overthinking, patient full takes with minimal overdubs. The lyrics were written only a few weeks before entering the studio to prevent the overall picture from being too fragmented and to increase the sense of risk and urgency. For Love of Grace s both fun and as serious as ever, growing and glowing through love. There is no affectation or prescription to this recordno palette of curated influence or sought sound. It is the sum total of inspirations, shared openly in the name of playing and playings pleasures.

title.en: Hannaford Street Silver presents April in Brass

ai.en: Hannaford Street Silver Band's April in Brass at Jane Mallett Theatre in Toronto, closing its 2026-27 season with new Canadian music, with the solo hornist Catherine Turner.

events.description: The Hannaford Street Silver Band concludes its 2026-27 season with April in Brass, a spectacular afternoon celebrating brass virtuosity, new Canadian music, and the remarkable versatility of the brass ensemble. Taking centre stage is Catherine Turner, solo hornist with the Orchestre symphonique de Montréal, performing Richard Strauss's magnificent Horn Concerto No. 1. Written in 1882-83 when Strauss was still a teenager, the concerto has become one of the defining works of the horn repertoire. Its soaring melodies, brilliant fanfares, lyrical passages, and demanding virtuosity make it an ideal showcase for the extraordinary colours and expressive possibilities of the horn. Turner brings her experience as a leading orchestral horn player to this exciting collaboration with Hannaford, creating an opportunity to hear one of the great works of the horn repertoire in a distinctive brass-band setting.

ai.en: Seven Heavens Away by Ashraf Zaghal, a By the Lake Book Club discussion at Assembly Hall.

events.description: Presented by: City of Toronto’s Assembly Hall, Humber Polytechnic’s Faculty of Media, Creative Arts and Design Seven Heavens Away is a coming-of-age novel set in Jerusalem, following a Palestinian teenager grappling with grief, identity and belonging after a close friend's death amid escalating violence. Navigating family, friendship and a complicated bond with a Jewish girl, he confronts hard questions about loss, hope and the future. Ashraf Zaghal will reflect on the novel's creative process, writing about memory and displacement, and how his characters illuminate identity, community and resilience. By the Lake Book Club offers six Tuesday-night events, between February and December featuring leading Canadian authors in conversation with Humber Polytechnics alumni. Each in-person event includes a reading, discussion, audience Q&A, book-signing and American sign language interpretation. Virtual events are subtitled live.

ai.en: The Sound of Spring: Beethoven, Elgar, Ho, an Orchestra Toronto concert at Meridian Arts Centre's George Weston Hall, opening with Alice Ho's Jubilation of Spring and including Elgar's Cello Concerto in E minor.

events.description: Orchestra Toronto celebrates the vibrancy of nature and human emotion in this program. The concert opens with Alice Ho?s Jubilation of Spring, a bright and dynamic work that captures the energy, color, and renewal of the season through inventive orchestral textures. Elgar?s Cello Concerto in E Minor, featuring Cellist Lucia Ticho, follows, a deeply introspective and lyrical masterpiece that showcases Ticho?s expressive range while conveying themes of loss, reflection, and hope. The program concludes with Beethoven?s Symphony No. 6, ?Pastoral?, a work that evokes the tranquility and rhythms of the countryside, celebrating humanity?s connection to the natural world with warmth, charm, and compositional ingenuity.

title.en: Music Toronto - Karen Ouzounian and Lembit Beecher's MAYRIG/MOTHER

ai.en: MAYRIG/MOTHER, by cellist Karen Ouzounian and composer-pianist Lembit Beecher, at the Jane Mallett Theatre for Music Toronto.

events.description: Cellist Karen Ouzounian, acclaimed for her work with the Silkroad Ensemble and the Aizuri Quartet, joins composer-pianist Lembit Beecher to close the season’s MUSE series with Mayrig, an immersive multimedia program centered on the human voice. Voices of Ouzounian’s mother and grandmother weave through Armenian music from Anatolia, songs of Lebanon, and the music of Charles Aznavour, alongside new works exploring memory, heritage, and resilience across generations. The program spans centuries and cultures, opening and closing with Marin Marais’s Les Voix Humaines. Traditional Armenian songs and early Anatolian recordings appear alongside arrangements of music by Charles Aznavour and Ashot Satyan. Original works by Lembit Beecher are joined by contemporary voices including Layale Chaker, Nathalie Joachim, Niloufar Nourbakhsh, and Karen Ouzounian, interwoven with recorded voices from Ouzounian’s family.
